items.title: Kind reminder- Bridging disciplines by the Mathematics and Economics Club
items.body:
Dear Students,

How does Mathematics shape the way we understand Economics? And how can a background in mathematics open doors to graduate studies and research in economics?

 Join the Mathematics Club and Economics Club at LAU for an engaging interdisciplinary event exploring the connection between these two fields! Whether you’re a
 mathematics enthusiast, an economics student, or simply curious about where these disciplines meet, this is an opportunity to explore new perspectives and possibilities!

Through insights from distinguished professors and the personal journeys of mathematics graduates who pursued PhDs in Economics, discover how mathematical foundations
 can lead to exciting academic and career opportunities.

Date: Friday, November 27, 2026

Time: 3:30–5:00 p.m.

Location: AKSOB 1211, LAU Beirut Campus

Online:

Speakers:

- Dr. Walid Marrouch, Professor of Economics and Associate Dean of Graduate Studies and Research
- Dr. Mohamad Karaki, Associate Professor of Economics
- Dr. Nour Chalhoub, Assistant Professor of Economics
- Dr. Ghina Abdul Baki, Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Ottawa

Please refer the flyer below for further details, and kindly confirm your participation though this
link.

We look forward to seeing you there!

Jamal

Jamal Ibrahim Haidar

items.title: Course Evaluations Fall 2026
items.body:
Dear Students,

Let your voice be heard. This is your chance to evaluate your learning experience at LAU.  You are kindly requested to complete the course evaluations between
November 28, 2026 and December 7, 2026. According to university policy, in case you do not fill out
all the course evaluations by December 7, 2026, you will not be able to access your final grades before
January 2, 2027.

General principles of course evaluations:

1.
Your responses will remain totally confidential and anonymous. Student identity cannot be linked to the course evaluation in any way.

2.
Courses that enroll less than three students are automatically excluded from the evaluation. The aim of this practice is to preserve the anonymity of respondents.

3.
The purpose of the evaluations is to improve your learning experience and the quality of education at the institution.

4.
Make sure you clearly read the instructions and questions and select the option that best expresses your opinion.

5.
Please fill the evaluation form, as this is your chance to voice the level of your satisfaction with the course and the teaching practices.

6.
Make sure to write comments that point out
good as well as bad practices you faced.

7.
The results of the course evaluation surveys will only be released to the faculty after all grades are posted, thus your feedback will not affect your grade.

8.
Note that you may access the questionnaire through your
email or the student portal. The emails (invitation and two reminders) have the “Department of Institutional Research” as a sender and “Course Evaluations – (Term)” as the subject line. Please check your junk mail and clutter folders in case you
 don’t receive the email.

9.
It is recommended you use Edge or Google Chrome to fill your course evaluations, particularly if you face latency issues.

10.
Course evaluations for courses that follow a regular schedule are administered at the end of each term. You will be invited to fill out your course evaluation in a span of 10 days prior to the start of the final
 exam period.

11.
Once you have submitted your course evaluations, access your link again and make sure that the word “completed” appears next to
each course.

12.
Make sure you complete all course evaluations. In case you receive a
reminder email requesting you to complete the course evaluations once you have clicked the submit button, then you most probably have not completed at least one course evaluation. You should access the course evaluation link again and complete all course
 evaluations.

Keep in mind that we appreciate your help in making this University a better place!

items.title: SOE Seminar Series | Demystifying AI: How Large Language Models Work | Monday, November 30, 2026 | Online via Webex
items.body:
Reminder: Join us
Monday, November 30, from 9:00 to 10:00 a.m., for the webinar
Demystifying AI: How Large Language Models Work by Dr. Tarek Sakakini, online via Webex.

Greetings,

As part of the
SOE seminar series, the School of Engineering is pleased to invite you to the webinar entitled “Demystifying AI: How Large Language Models Work”.

The seminar details are as follows:

🎤
Speaker: Dr. Tarek Sakakini, Lecturer, California State University – Sacramento.

📄
Title: Demystifying AI: How Large Language Models Work

📅
Date: Monday, November 30, 2026

🕒
Time: 09:00 a.m. – 10:00 a.m.

📍
Place: Online via Webex

Abstract:

What happens behind the scenes when you ask ChatGPT a question? This interactive, nontechnical talk explains how large language models work, starting with the simple idea of predicting the next
 word. Through familiar examples and audience participation, we explore how models learn from text and how prompting turns text prediction into useful conversations. We then examine why AI used to hallucinate, how it accesses information beyond its training
 data, and how features such as tools, memory, and reasoning fit into the picture. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of the technology behind today’s AI assistants, their capabilities, and their limitations. No prior background in AI or programming
 is required.

About the Speaker:

Dr. Tarek Sakakini teaches computer science and artificial intelligence at California State University, Sacramento, and Folsom Lake College. He earned his Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering
 from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, specializing in natural language processing and machine learning, and his undergraduate engineering degree from the American University of Beirut. Previously, he worked as an Applied Scientist in Amazon’s Artificial
 General Intelligence organization, developing language model capabilities for Alexa. His experience also includes research at Apple and IBM, with work spanning conversational AI and educational applications. His delivery emphasizes making complex technical
 ideas accessible and helping students build understanding from first principles.

items.title: SOE Seminar Series | The Future of Work: Exploring how Artificial Intelligence, Agentic AI, and workflow automation are reshaping the way organizations operate | Wednesday, December 2, 2026
items.body:
Greetings,

As part of the SOE seminar series, the School of Engineering is pleased to invite you to the semester entitled “ The Future of Work:
 Exploring how Artificial Intelligence, Agentic AI, and workflow automation are reshaping the way organizations operate ”.

The seminar details are as follows:

🎤
Lead Speaker: Mr. Charbel Akkad, Partner & Principal Consultant Interphase

      Speakers: Mr. Mohamad Abdul Hadi, Senior Software Engineer Interphase

                        Mr. Mohamad Saad, Senior Software Engineer Interphase

                        Ms. Nourhane Jundi, Senior Software Engineer Interphase

📄
Title: The Future of Work: Exploring how Artificial Intelligence, Agentic AI, and workflow automation are reshaping the way organizations operate

📅
Date: Wednesday, December 2, 2026

🕒
Time: 01:00 p.m. – 02:00 p.m.

📍
Place: Chagoury Medical Auditorium, Byblos Campus

The seminar will cover:

- The evolution from traditional automation to AI-powered and agentic workflows.
- Practical applications of AI in business operations and digital transformation.
- The technologies and approaches behind intelligent workflow automation.
- Real-world use cases and demonstrations through Populus, Interphase's AI-powered business transformation platform.
- Emerging opportunities and industry-relevant skills for engineering students.

We look forward to seeing you all there!

Abstract:

Artificial Intelligence is rapidly evolving beyond traditional analytical applications, becoming an active component of how organizations manage processes, make decisions, and execute everyday operations. This seminar explores
 the convergence of Artificial Intelligence, workflow automation, and emerging Agentic AI technologies, highlighting how these innovations are transforming traditional business operations into intelligent, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous processes.

Drawing on Interphase's experience in developing and implementing digital transformation solutions, the session will bridge theoretical concepts with practical industry applications. Participants will discover how AI capabilities
 can be integrated into business workflows, how intelligent automation can improve operational efficiency, and how organizations are moving toward more connected and data-driven operating models. The seminar will also feature practical demonstrations and real-world
 use cases powered by Populus, Interphase's AI business transformation platform, illustrating how modern technologies can be applied to solve operational challenges.

Beyond the technology itself, the session will highlight emerging opportunities for engineering students, the evolving skills required in an AI-driven industry, and the importance of connecting academic knowledge with practical
 innovation.

About the Speaker:

Charbel Akkad is a Partner and Principal Consultant at Interphase, a technology and consulting company specializing in digital transformation, business process automation, and AI-powered solutions. With over seven years of
 experience in the ICT and digital transformation sector, Charbel has contributed to technology-driven projects across Lebanon and the GCC, working with public and private sector organizations to improve operational efficiency and accelerate digital transformation.

Any LAU student from any major or year. Selection is made by the project faculty.

A unique, long-term, multidisciplinary program where you join faculty-led teams with possible industry co-mentors to work on real projects, build technical and professional skills, and even explore entrepreneurial pathways.

- Juniors: : 1 or 2 Credits per semester (VIP301, VIP302)
- Seniors: : 1 or 2 Credits per semester (VIP401, VIP402)

items.title: SOE Research Track Certificate of Completion
items.body:
Dear SOE Students,

As you prepare your Spring 2027 course schedule, we invite you to consider pursuing the
Research Track and earning its Certificate of Completion. The track is designed for undergraduate students who want to go beyond the traditional curriculum through meaningful faculty-supervised research.

To qualify for the certificate, students must complete:

-
6 credits of Undergraduate Research Experience (URE).
-
The 3-credit course GNE598 Research Methods for Engineers.

GNE598 will be offered in Spring 2027. Students may enroll once they have completed 3 credits of URE or are concurrently registered in 3 credits of URE. The course builds core research skills, including conducting a literature review, formulating research
 questions, practicing research ethically, and writing proposals and research papers.

Why join the Research Track?

-
Hands-on experience working closely with faculty on real research problems.

-
A formal certificate that documents your research training and sets your profile apart.

-
Stronger applications for graduate programs and fast-track PhD pathways.
-
A competitive edge for fellowships, scholarships and R&D careers.

Further information is available at Research Track Certificate of Completion. For inquiries, feel free to contact the SOE Dean’s Office at (dean.soe@lau.edu.lb).
